note: Countries and homelands beyond the United States. Each listing is read from the organization's own page or a government page, written in plain words, with its source and the date it was checked.

countries.name: United States
countries.peoples: American Indian, Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian peoples

countries.name: Canada
countries.intro: Canada recognizes three groups of Indigenous peoples in its Constitution: First Nations, Inuit and Métis. The map shows the administrative office of every First Nation registered with Indigenous Services Canada and every Inuit community, from the Government of Canada's open data. Each First Nation links to its official profile, which has its address and phone.

intro_sources.label: Indigenous Services Canada: First Nations Location (open data)

urgent.label: Hope for Wellness, for all Indigenous people

countries.name: México
countries.peoples: Pueblos indígenas y el pueblo afromexicano
countries.intro: Mexico's National Institute of Indigenous Peoples (INPI) counts 68 Indigenous peoples and the Afro-Mexican people. About 25.7 million people in Mexico identify as Indigenous, and 7.4 million speak an Indigenous language.

intro_sources.label: INPI: el INPI, institución al servicio de los pueblos indígenas y afromexicanos (2020)

countries.name: Australia
countries.peoples: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
countries.intro: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people run their own health services across Australia: Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisations, started and governed by the local community. The first opened in Redfern, Sydney, in 1971. There is also a national crisis line answered by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

intro_sources.label: NACCHO (via the Royal Australian College of GPs)

urgent.label: 13YARN, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander crisis support

countries.name: Aotearoa New Zealand
countries.intro: Te Kāhui Māngai, run by Te Puni Kōkiri (the Ministry of Māori Development), is the government's directory of iwi, hapū and marae and the organizations that represent them. Whānau Ora navigators help whānau plan and reach the support they need.

intro_sources.label: Te Puni Kōkiri: Whānau Ora for whānau

urgent.label: Need to talk? Free call or text, any time

countries.name: Sápmi (Norway, Sweden, Finland)
countries.intro: The Sámi are an Indigenous people whose homeland, Sápmi, stretches across northern Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia. Each of the three Nordic countries has an elected Sámi Parliament. The Sámi Parliament of Finland notes that the Sámi are the only Indigenous people in the European Union.

countries.name: Brasil
countries.intro: The Fundação Nacional dos Povos Indígenas (Funai) is the Brazilian state's official Indigenous agency. Its mission is to protect and promote the rights of Indigenous peoples in Brazil, and its headquarters are in Brasília.

countries.name: Perú
countries.intro: Peru officially recognizes 47 Indigenous languages, spoken by 55 peoples. In the 2017 census almost six million people, just over a quarter of the population, identified as Indigenous; most identified as Quechua or Aymara.

urgent.label: Línea 113 Salud, opción 5: salud mental (24 horas, gratuita)

countries.name: Guatemala
countries.intro: More than four in ten people in Guatemala are Indigenous, most of them from the Maya peoples, among them the K'iche', Kaqchikel, Mam and Q'eqchi'. Guatemala's population was projected at 18.8 million for 2025, 43.75% of them Indigenous.

countries.name: Chile
countries.intro: Chile's Indigenous Law (Ley 19.253) of 1993 recognizes nine Indigenous peoples and created the National Corporation for Indigenous Development (CONADI), which runs Indigenous development programs and has its national office in Temuco.

intro_sources.label: CONADI: Dirección Regional Osorno, perfil de cargo (Servicio Civil)

urgent.label: Línea de prevención del suicidio *4141 (24 horas, gratuita, desde celulares)

countries.name: Kalaallit Nunaat (Greenland)
countries.intro: Kalaallit Nunaat has governed itself since 1979 within the Kingdom of Denmark. Of its 56,740 people (February 2026), 88.9% are Greenlandic Inuit, most of whom call themselves Kalaallit. About 17,000 Kalaallit live in Denmark.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.intro: Taiwan officially recognizes 16 Indigenous peoples, who numbered 629,456 people, 2.7% of the population, at the end of 2025. They are represented at every level of government, including the central government's Council of Indigenous Peoples. Lowland Pingpu peoples are still seeking recognition.

urgent.label: 1925 Care Hotline, suicide prevention (24 hours, free)

countries.name: Japan
countries.intro: Japan has two Indigenous peoples: the Ainu in the far north and the Ryūkyūans (Okinawans) in the far south. The Ainu have been officially recognized as an Indigenous people since June 2008. Upopoy, the national center for Ainu history and culture, opened in Shiraoi, Hokkaido, in July 2020.

intro_sources.label: Government of Japan: Experience the Ainu world

countries.name: Philippines
countries.intro: The 2020 census counted 9,841,785 Indigenous people in the Philippines: 63% in Mindanao, where the Lumad are the largest group, 34% in Luzon and 3% in the Visayas. The National Commission on Indigenous Peoples was created under the Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act of 1997.

countries.name: Botswana
countries.intro: Botswana's government does not recognize any specific group as Indigenous, holding that all citizens are. But 3.41% of people identify with an Indigenous group, among them about 76,231 San (called Basarwa in Botswana), the Balala and the Nama.

countries.name: Namibia
countries.peoples: San, Ovahimba, Ovatue, Ovatjimba and others
countries.intro: Namibia's Indigenous peoples include the San groups, the Ovatue, Ovahimba and Ovatjimba, and possibly others such as the Nama and Topnaars. Together they are less than 3% of the population. More than 80% of the San have lost their ancestral lands.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.intro: The Khoikhoi and San peoples (the Khoisan) identify as South Africa's Indigenous peoples. Their largest representative bodies are the National Khoisan Council and the San Council of South Africa. Full legal recognition is still incomplete.

countries.name: Worldwide
countries.intro: Help that reaches Indigenous peoples in any country: international bodies and funds led by Indigenous people.
